"Let's say the team that finished 18th would've finished 17th if Manchester City weren't there. And they, of course, suffered huge loss. If you add all those claims up, over nine years, and that's just in the Premier League, you can see that the potential here for this to spiral out of control is huge."

‌



View 4 Images Noel pictured in the stands after a City game this month (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

Mr Purslow added: "I really hope that common sense prevails here and that there is a comprehensive solution between the authorities and Manchester City that looks at all these issues and tries to draw a line in the sand. Because a never-ending waterfall of legal claims and uncertainties for another four or five years would be absolutely appalling for the game."

Writing on X, Noel's younger brother Liam, 54, today wrote: "We'll win the appeal and all the WETWIPES from other clubs begging for our titles need to sit down... embarrassing."

‌



The alleged breaches took place between the 2009-10 and 2022-23 seasons, during which time Man City won seven Premier League titles, a Champions League, three FA Cups and six League Cups. They relate to a number of areas, with the most serious linked to claims the club failed to provide “accurate financial information” to the league.

They were accused of a wide range of rule breaches centring on claims they inflated sponsorship revenue from connected companies and made other "off the books" payments to circumvent football's financial rules.

Uefa previously found Man City in breach of football fair play rules in 2014, a decision that resulted in the club paying a €20m fine. By 2020, Uefa had suspended City from the Champions League for “overstating its sponsorship revenue in its accounts”. But the suspension was later overturned by the club on appeal to the court of arbitration for sport.

‌



View 4 Images Erling Haaland is one of Manchester City's stars (Image: Getty Images)

The Premier League or Man City, whose executives are said to have signed non-disclosure agreements, have so far refused to publicly confirm the latest alleged verdicts.

A Man City spokesperson said: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

‌



“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

'Our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began'

In an open letter today published on Man City's website, the club's chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak wrote: "Following Friday’s media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here’s what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies. "I ask you to please carefully read the statement below, which we gave on Friday, and the statement we issued in February 2023. Every word matters and holds true.

Article continues below

"While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our Club. We will not give them that opportunity.

Arsenal fan Piers Morgan today wrote on X: "Let’s be clear: Manchester City have been found guilty of being the biggest cheats in English football history, and the punishment must fit their crimes. At very minimum, they must be relegated from Premier League and stripped of all fraudulently ‘won’ titles."

Former Man City chairman David Bernstein told Times Radio: “I’m a fan of Manchester City and have been a fan for 70 years. “First of all, the timing of this I think is crucial. This whole process has taken too long already. So the appeal process now has to be done quickly because…you’ve got the club playing with this cloud over its head and it’s just not viable. “I can’t give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of 115 charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty. All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that.”

News.title: Man City chairman insists club are INNOCENT in letter after 115 charges verdict
News.content:
Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the chairman of Manchester City, has once again stressed the club remain confident of proving their innocence in the wake of reports claiming they have been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges laid against them.

Media reports emerged on Friday afternoon outlining that a verdict had been reached in the case against the former Premier League champions, though no official statement confirming such an outcome has yet been released.

But Al Mubarak has now broken his silence - and he remains insistent that the club are confident of clearing their name.

"I have been part of this Club for 18 years," Al Mubarak wrote in a statement shared on the club website on Saturday afternoon.

‌

"I have had the privilege to stand with you in the Etihad, at Wembley, and in Istanbul. This Club matters to me, and you have shown and told me – time and time again - how much Manchester City matters to you. This is why I am writing to you today.

"Following Friday’s media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here’s what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

‌



"I ask you to please carefully read the statement below, which we gave on Friday, and the statement we issued in February 2023. Every word matters and holds true.

View 2 Images Al Mubarak has overseen a period of domestic dominance for Manchester City (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

"While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our Club. We will not give them that opportunity.

"We have some exciting moments to look forward to after this international break. We travel to Anfield in a fortnight, and then host Paris St Germain in the Champions League back at Etihad Stadium - moments that give us an opportunity to celebrate the strength of the Manchester City family.

‌



"Thank you, as always, for your constant support."

A club statement was also attached below Al Mubarak's words, stressing that the process remains ongoing and that the club's position remains as it was back in February 2023.

City's statement continued: "The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

News.title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham is to introduce a new scheme to try to help young people get on the property ladder.

The "Your First Home" scheme would be open to first-time buyers in England with a deposit of 2.5%. It would provide them with a loan worth 20% of their new build property's value to help pay for the purchase.

Burnham said people who do not have support from the "bank of mum and dad" are among those the scheme would aim to help.

Labour said there would be an initial interest-free period for the equity loan. Further details on the scheme are expected in next month's Budget and pre-registration will open before the end of the year.

Burnham said: "Too many young people are struggling with the cost of housing, with many giving up hope of ever having a home to call their own.

"So we will step in to help more first-time buyers onto the housing ladder."

The PM added he believes the scheme will give builders the "confidence to deliver the high-quality new homes the country needs".

Funding for the scheme is expected to come from reprioritising existing budgets; but housing developers will pay towards the running costs.

Ministers have not yet confirmed whether there is an age restriction on the scheme, or a cap on the price on the value of the property.

The announcement came as Burnham arrived in Liverpool ahead of his first Labour Party conference since becoming prime minister.

The policy is similar to initiatives from previous governments, including the coalition's Help To Buy scheme, introduced in 2013 by then-Chancellor George Osborne.

It expanded a previous scheme, known as FirstBuy, which was aimed solely at first-time buyers.

Help to Buy initially enabled all purchasers to put down a 5% deposit on a newly built home. Up to 20% of the cost of the home was funded by a shared equity loan, which was interest-free for the first five years.

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner said Your First Home would "build on the lessons learned from previous schemes, while retaining the benefits".

"We're delivering a new generation of equity loans in a Labour way, targeting support to those first-time buyers who need support the most," she said.

Rayner told the BBC earlier this month that there was only a "slim chance" the government would meet its target of building 1.5m homes in England by the next election, but said she was "not giving it up".

Data up to June this year suggested the government was behind on the rate of construction needed to meet the goal, which housebuilders have previously warned was too optimistic.

BBC Verify analysis showed a decline in the number of new houses being built during Labour's first year in power - continuing a fall that began under the Conservatives.

News.title: Heathrow Airport warns third runway could be delayed by four years
News.content:
Heathrow Airport has warned that its planned third runway might be delayed by four years due to planning and regulatory issues.

The government had hoped the new runway at the UK's busiest airport, estimated to cost Â£33bn, would open by 2035.

But Heathrow sees this deadline as increasingly difficult to deliver without further steps to simplify the planning process. It said on Saturday that it hoped to secure planning permission by 2029 and then open the runway "within a decade".

The Department for Transport (DfT) said the project's timeline had "always been ambitious" and that it would continue to work with stakeholders "at pace" on the matter.

The airport said its "core scenario" had always been to open a new runway within a decade of securing planning permission.

It said it was encouraged by the chancellor's efforts to streamline infrastructure and remove regulatory bottlenecks, and promised to continue to work with ministers, airlines and stakeholders to "progress the planning application with pace".

Former chancellor Rachel Reeves announced the government's support for the project in January 2025 as a means to grow the economy, and Prime Minister Andy Burnham - who was previously critical - said he was "open-minded" about the scheme when he came to office.

Despite attracting wide opposition from environmental campaigners and local resident groups, the project is expected to create around 100,000 jobs and provide a major boost to the economy as part of a wider Â£49bn modernisation of the airport.

The expansion would mean demolishing hundreds of homes, diverting rivers, and rerouting the M25 motorway between junctions 14 and 15 through a tunnel under the new runway.

The number of flights from the site, currently capped at 480,000 a year, could go up to 720,000 - or nearly 2,000 a day on average.

News.title: How long can Labour's feel-good factor last?
News.content:
"He just loves being prime minister," a government insider observes.

Andy Burnham might not yet have delivered his all-important conference speech, but he has been preparing for this moment for years.

He'll lap up the inevitable whoops and cheers â not just as Labour's leader, but the kind of leader who chimes with the party's rank and file, who puts social justice at the top of his list, who is not averse to cranking up the greatest hits â whether taking a pop at Mrs Thatcher, privatisation, or the divides between north and south.

Speaking to MPs, ministers and advisers inside the party, there is no doubt whatsoever that Labour is in a much, much happier place than this time last year.

There is a very simple reason, according to one cabinet minister, fans of Sir Keir Starmer, look away now, "people like the new prime minister more than they liked the old one â that's the truth of it".

Another minister tells me: "There is no appetite for destruction â very little naysaying."

But Labour is in a position that's been all too rare for all our political parties in the last few years â there are no whispers about chucking out the leader, no-one stirring revolt.

And even those who don't like the direction of travel are labelling their opinions as a desire to be helpful, they're not trying to criticise the boss.

"The mood's good â everyone is going into conference with their ears open," one MP said, keen to hear more from the prime minister.

The feel-good factor is also driven by the party inching up a little in the polls â one senior figure says: "We're all witnessing the Burnham bounce â whether that's how you feel when you see the polls, or how we all feel when we have meetings together."

News.title: Met to re-examine CCTV from Jill Dando murder case
News.content:
The Met Police has confirmed it will re-examine CCTV footage relating to the unsolved murder of Jill Dando, 27 years ago.

The BBC presenter and journalist was shot dead with a single bullet on her doorstep in Fulham in April 1999. Despite one of the biggest and most high-profile murder investigations in British history, the case remains unsolved.

A Met spokesperson said recent advancements in CCTV enhancement technology had "provided investigators with the opportunity to re-examine original footage from Putney Bridge train station".

The CCTV includes an unidentified man who was seen sprinting near the scene of the shooting, 20 minutes after the event.

The Met said in the 27 years since Dando's death, the investigation had been "subject to numerous reviews", aiming to identify whether matters could be progressed with advances in technology and forensics.

It warned this latest review was part of "ongoing inquiries and should not be interpreted as a significant line of inquiry nor as a new investigation being opened on this matter".

News.title: Republic of Ireland to wear black armbands for Israel game
News.content:
Republic of Ireland players intend to wear black armbands "in recognition of all lives lost in the [Gaza] conflict" for Sunday's Nations League game against Israel in Hungary, after confirming they will go ahead with the fixture.

Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell confirmed one player has withdrawn from the squad before the match.

But he added that a vote among the squad produced a "significant majority" in favour of playing.

As well as the intention to wear black armbands for Sunday's 'away' game against Israel in Debrecen, Courell said the players will make further gestures for the initial game and the return 'home' fixture against Israel next Sunday in Serbia.

The fixtures have been embroiled in controversy since the two teams were drawn to play each other in Group B3.

Republic of Ireland players faced calls to withdraw from the games because of the ongoing Israel-Gaza war with a "Stop The Game" campaign - organised by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine - gathering pace.

"One of their requests is to remove their media obligations for the remainder of this window," Courell said at Saturday's delayed news conference.

"They also have the intention to wear black armbands in recognition of all lives lost in the [Gaza] conflict.

"There will be elements of the pre-match ceremony not be partaken in by the Republic of Ireland and it is also the intention of the players to make a significant contribution to charitable donation by virtue of both [Israel] match fees and also the fixture against Austria at the Aviva [Stadium in Dublin on Thursday]."

News.title: Watch: Prince Harry says 'kids are happy' in British school after six years in US
News.content:
The Duke of Sussex has said it feels "great" to be back in Britain after spending six years living in California.

He told Canadian network CTV: "It's been great. It's been great to be back on British soil. The kids are happy in school and it gives me a chance to be able to really focus on the Invictus Games in Birmingham in July next year."

Prince Harry and Meghan stepped back as senior royals and began a new life in the US in 2020, before returning to live in Britain last month.

It is thought the family are basing themselves at a private property outside of London in the Cotswolds area.

The couple's children, Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five, had to be moved to a different school only days after they started over security concerns about the school run.

It is understood that the Sussexes' private security team had raised concerns about the distance and heavy traffic on the route to the school.

Harry and Meghan's return to the UK has been marked by tensions with the Royal Family.

News.title: How the bare nails trend became a class issue
News.content:
And when waves of Vietnamese refugees gave rise to the nail bar in the 1970s, professional manicures were no longer the preserve of the rich.

But, like many luxuries, as they became more popular and more accessible to the masses, the wealthy began pivoting â a textbook example of behaviour known as "counter signalling", Rudolfo says.

"The same way that logo bags are considered gauche or quiet luxury is more aspirational, bare nails are considered the trend now.

"The examples are almost always white women or celebrities... [and] they'll often conflate class and taste with that bareness."

Others point out bare nails often demand their own time-consuming and costly routine.

"The irony in all this is these natural nails are not natural either," Shapiro says. "They also require a lot of grooming and sometimes pretty premiere services."

Few would argue there aren't valid feminist questions for the beauty industry to answer, around unrealistic standards for example, but the largely female-run nail sector also feels empowering for many women.

"I feel like nail care has very much had a 'for women, by women' sort of ethos around it," Shapiro says. "The first salon opened in New York City was owned by a woman, and she was a remarkably independent one... a lot of the first entrepreneurs offering product lines, opening salons were women."

Hampton admits she's saddened by the way trends have been â and continue to be - weaponised.

"We're taking the fun out of nails... Anyone should be able to wear what they like - nail polish or bare nails," she says. "Why is there an argument? Why is there beef?"

Scanlon too is a little baffled.

"For me, it's like, just stop judging ourselves and everybody else," she says. "Some people like to have the nails done, some people don't.

"I suppose the question that I was posing was, is it doing anything for you?

"The truth of it is: it's not that deep."

News.title: Your child has left home. Here's why it's time to stop checking up on them
News.content:
"Sometimes parents send their child to university and they're not even worried, but then these group chats create a worry that something might be wrong," says Rayyah Uddin, 20, a third-year student at the University of Nottingham.

She knows of WhatsApp group chats being set up by parents of first-year students at her university and has also seen parents use TikTok to share their worries about their child not making friends, and asking other parents for their help.

"These are issues the students should really be figuring out for themselves, and it is better if parents try and talk to their child rather than immediately jump to other parents," she says.

Not hearing from your child all the time isn't necessarily a cause for concern - "they might just be having a really good time and are getting absorbed into university life," Rayyah adds.

Parent social media groups can be useful, according to psychologist Charlotte Armitage, but not when they are used to share private difficulties, track movements or ask questions that the student is capable of asking themselves.

"Constant checking, tracking or intervening may soothe the parent in the short term, but it can inadvertently communicate to the young adult: 'I am not sure you can cope without me.'"

"Of course, where there is a credible safeguarding concern, a significant change in behaviour, or a known risk to their wellbeing, parents should act."

News.title: Man City chairman confident club will prove innocence
News.content:
Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak says he is still confident of proving the club's innocence after they were found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules.

City were accused of a wide range of rule breaches, centring around claims they inflated sponsorship revenue from connected companies and made other "off the books" payments to circumvent financial regulations.

On Friday, it was announced City had been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges brought against them and Al Mubarak has responded with a letter to fans on the club's website.

"Following Friday's media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I," Al Mubarak said.

"Here's what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position.

"But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies."

Premier League clubs are seeking legal advice about compensation relating to the charges, while BBC Sport has been told City will appeal.

Sanctions on the club are yet to be announced, but repercussions could include a points deduction, expulsion from the Premier League or a huge fine.

Al Mubarak, who was appointed as City's chairman after their 2008 takeover, also said his club was being "undermined".

"While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed," he added.

"There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity."

News.title: 'No turning back' in independence journey, says first minister at rally
News.content:
Wales' first minister has said there is "no turning back" on the journey to independence for the country, as he attended a rally on Saturday.

In a speech addressing the crowd gathered in Aberystwyth, Ceredigion, Rhun ap Iorwerth said the "next step" for Wales had to be "equality with Scotland, as a minimum".

Thousands were in attendance, with the event organisers, campaign group Yes Cymru, saying it estimated the march attracted between 8,000 and 9,000 people.

"[Wales is] on a journey, and there's no turning back," ap Iorwerth said.

Since 2019, thousands have taken part in independence marches across Wales, including in Cardiff, Swansea, Wrexham, Merthyr Tydfil, Rhyl and Barry.

But this was the first time the first minister of Wales had attended a Yes Cymru march.

A Reform Cymru Member of the Senedd (MS) said he was "disappointed" by the first minister's decision to attend, while a Welsh Conservative MS said it would be "better for him to be behind his desk in Cathays sorting the problems he said he would sort out".

News.title: High Court grants injunction to stop Orange Order Drumcree parade
News.content:
Earlier on Saturday Judge Smyth had given the parties involved a final opportunity to "reach an agreement" and "step back from the abyss".

Following an adjournment she requested that the lodge was contacted to find out whether it would be prepared to temporarily halt the parade to allow a full hearing to take place.

In response, the lodge submitted a two-page letter to the court and while the details were not read out, the judge indicated there was "no agreement" to delay the march.

Judge Smyth requested that lawyers for the individual Orangeman contact the rest of the lodge to seek their view.

The judge said the lodge should be informed of the issues the court is dealing with and asked whether they would agree not to proceed "for a matter of days" to allow for an informed judgment to be facilitated.

Adjourning the case for a third time on Saturday, Judge Smyth said "it is my view the issues at stake are so sensitive and so important, I would expect all of the lawyers to be creative and to use the law for the good of all the people in Northern Ireland."

Judge Smyth said the issue the court is dealing with is of "fundamental importance" to the entire society in Northern Ireland.

News.title: Mayfair club shuts as Met investigates weapon claim
News.content:
A private members' club popular with celebrities has temporarily closed while police investigate allegations of threatening behaviour and whether a weapon was brandished in a nearby street.

The Metropolitan Police said it asked Westminster City Council to review Maison Estelle's alcohol licence as the premises was "allegedly associated with serious crime, or serious disorder, or both".

It related to an incident on 19 September, the force said. No injuries were reported.

Councillors suspended the licence at a private hearing on Thursday. The Mayfair venue, which has hosted Princess Beatrice, Idris Elba and Kim Kardashian, said it would be closed for "a few weeks" while investigations took place.

"A further hearing will be held in due course," a Met spokesperson said.

"The circumstances remain under investigation, including whether a firearm â or imitation firearm â was involved."

News.title: E-motorbikes seized by police sold on at auction, BBC finds
News.content:
Electric motorbikes seized by police forces in the UK are being sold on at auction, despite some fears they could end up back in the hands of criminals, the BBC can reveal.

Thousands are confiscated annually because they are suspected of being driven illegally, or used in a crime - most are later destroyed, but a BBC investigation has found some are sold on to members of the public in online auctions.

Across the UK, police sold 161 e-bikes and e-motorcycles last year and 54 in 2024, although the real number could be higher because not every force responded to the BBC's Freedom of Information request.

Some of the forces said they had now ended the practice, but others defended it as a way of putting "money back into policing".

Six forces responded to say some of the vehicles they had seized had been sold, including large forces such as West Midlands Police and Police Scotland.

The figure includes electrically-assisted pedal cycles, which look similar to bicycles and have a motor that kicks in as a rider pedals, as well as electric motorbikes, which are usually more powerful and are propelled only by their motor.

E-bikes and e-motorcycles have become controversial because some think they are linked to crime and anti-social behaviour.

Recent BBC reporting has highlighted cases across the country of balaclava-clad young men riding illegally on footpaths and intimidating residents.

There have also been a number of pedestrian deaths, including 86-year-old grandmother Gloria Stephenson, who was struck at a zebra crossing in Sunderland last year by an illegal e-motorbike.

News.title: Rayner criticises visa rule proposals ahead of Labour conference
News.content:
Before he became prime minister, Burnham said he "understood" where Rayner was coming from on her criticisms of the migrant visa changes, telling reporters in June that Labour "would do well to listen to what Angela has to say".

Rayner's call for a change of approach has been echoed by York Central Labour MP Rachael Maskell, who also wants a rethink from the home secretary.

She told the Today programme that "technically and morally" what is being proposed represented "the wrong set of values" and would affect "people who have come [to Britain] to serve faithfully and are then told that they have to wait another 10 years" to secure British citizenship.

In recent weeks, trade unions have put pressure on the government to soften its proposals, and a letter to Mahmood jointly signed by dozens of Labour MPs at the start of the year described the plans as "un-British".

Lisa Nandy, secretary of state for culture, media and sport, rejected the "un-British" description of the plans.

She told BBC Radio 4's Today programme: "I don't think they are un-British because I don't think that we have ever had an automatic right to citizenship for most people who come to the UK from overseas."

Nandy said the home secretary was trying to balance respect for people "regardless of who they or where they stand" with the need for "an immigration system that people have confidence in".

Asked if Labour could change its mind on the proposals, she told Today: "We always reserve the right to change our minds but we also will reserve the right to stick to our plans if we think we are getting them right".

The culture secretary said the government will not "change the rules of the game" in a way that unfairly disadvantages migrants who have contributed to the UK.

She said it would "strike the right balance" between treating people "fairly and decently as human beings but making sure there is an asylum and immigration system people can have confidence in."

Nandy's comments are a hint the government is reconsidering. She could have given a full-throated defence of the principle of backdating the changes so they apply to those foreign workers already here.

But she did not. Instead she emphasised the principle of those "contributing" to the UK and treating them fairly.

But if the government does reverse course on applying these changes to those arriving from 2021, the large numbers who came to the UK after that date have a quicker and easier route to settlement. That is a dividing line with the Conservatives and Reform UK that those parties will be keen to highlight.

The home secretary faced questions about the changes during an appearance at the Home Affairs Committee earlier this month.

Mahmood said she was "very aware that a large group of people who arrived in 2022, absent any change, would qualify in February 2027" for permanent settlement.

She added: "Later this year we will set out the new policy on settlement... as well as any transitional arrangements we might decide to implement."

News.title: WW2 sailor who lied about his age to sign up dies aged 101
News.content:
One of the West of England's last surviving veterans from World War Two has passed away aged 101.

Harry Francis, from South Gloucestershire, joined the Royal Navy in 1942 at 16, having lied about his age to serve.

He went on to join the Royal Marines and became one of the first men to join the Special Boat Service (SBS), carrying out covert operations in Italy, Lebanon and Burma (now known as Myanmar), where he was wounded.

His wife Gwen Francis said his family was "heartbroken" and "grateful for all the kindness people have shown" them.

News.title: Memorial for pupils contaminated with HIV and hepatitis
News.content:
The memorial installed at the college, near Alton, Hampshire, depicts two pupils, one with a sling and and another holding a cane, embracing each other.

Adrian Goodyear, 55, who first attended Treloar's when he was nine, said: "We couldn't believe the place we were looking at. Rolling country hills, swimming pools, canoes, a Jacobian mansion. It was just remarkable at first.

"We left school with death sentences."

Goodyear was infected with hepatitis and HIV while at the school.

"In 1985, a doctor tearfully said that I had two to three years to live," he explained.

"I was told this with five other boys and the doctor went round the room and said: 'You haveâ¦ you haven'tâ¦ you haveâ¦ you haven'tâ¦ you have got HIV'."

He said the memorial was important to keep the scandal "in the public consciousness" and to honour those who died.

He added: "When we were here we made promisesâ¦ they died in front of us, one winter we lost five boys.

"I made promises to them, as did the other lads here today, that we would never give up. We would find out what happened."

If you've been affected by the issues in this story, help and support is available via the BBC Action Line.

Several British adventurers, including Ben Fogle and Bear Grylls, have rallied around Sir Ranulph Fiennes amid concerns over his care.

A care home owner in Wales, where the 82-year-old explorer had been placed for seven weeks this year, told The Telegraph they had reported several concerns about Sir Ranulph’s wellbeing to the authorities, including the police.

The same newspaper claimed to have seen an email sent by a care watchdog that reportedly said Sir Ranulph was being unlawfully kept in care homes and unable to consent to his care or treatment.

TV presenter and adventurer Mr Fogle said he was “deeply disturbed” by the reports about Sir Ranulph’s care and urged an investigation.

He wrote on social media: “That such a great man, hero of mine and a national treasure, should be treated in this way, isolated and kept away from family and friends, is very troubling. It is time for the Office for the Public Guardian and the police to investigate this case.”

Mr Grylls also joined calls for police and the OPG to investigate, saying he and others had been “desperately trying to connect with Ran for a year now to no avail”.

open image in gallery Bear Grylls said he had failed to get in contact with Sir Ranulph for over a year ( @BearGrylls/X )

He said: “Ran is a true British icon for so many around the world – a pioneer, a humble warrior and a good friend to so many of us. He never failed to support me when I needed help. Now is our time.

“These reports of his isolation from his loved ones and treatment in care homes are so deeply disturbing. That a hero like Ran should have to face this is very hard to read. It’s past time for the Office for the Public Guardian and the police to investigate urgently. We owe it to him. Ran we are coming!”

open image in gallery Monty Don said an investigation into Sir Ranulph’s care was ‘vital’ ( PA )

BBC Gardeners’ World presenter Monty Don said: “My family and I have known Ran for over 40 years and he is one of the most inspirational, remarkable – and kindest – of men I have known. And of course, other than personal affection, he should be enjoying the admiration and respect of the whole country after such a remarkable life and not kept hidden away from family and friends.

“If anyone can be called a national treasure it is Ran and I do feel that it is vital that the OPG urgently investigates his case and all the facts can be brought to light.”

Gini Bowring, whose father Anton Bowring is Sir Ranulph’s business partner and long-standing friend, said: “Through all your expeditions and adventures, even in the most inhospitable places on Earth, we knew where you were,” according to The Telegraph.

“We knew how you were. If you needed help, we knew how to reach you. For two years, there has been silence. One minute you were there, the next…gone, unreachable!

“We don’t know where you are or how you are. We have tried to find you, and are still trying. We’re all hoping that the place where you should be safest has not become the hardest place you have ever had to face.”

open image in gallery The Care Inspectorate of Wales reportedly said Sir Ranulph was being ‘unlawfully deprived of his liberty’ ( Getty )

A spokesperson for the Care Inspectorate of Wales, which The Telegraph reported declared in an email to the Welsh care home owner that Sir Ranulph was being “unlawfully deprived of his liberty”, said: “Care Inspectorate Wales is committed to promoting the safety, wellbeing and rights of people who receive social care services across Wales.

“As part of this role, CIW monitors Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DoLS) to help ensure people living in care homes are protected and any restrictions placed on their freedom are lawful, necessary and in their best interests.

“Where a person is under continuous supervision and control, is not free to leave, and lacks the capacity to consent to their care arrangements, providers must apply to the local authority for a DoLS authorisation and notify CIW when an application has been made.

“It would not be appropriate for us to comment on an individual's personal circumstances or care arrangements.”

People without support from the “bank of mum and dad” to purchase their first home will get access to a new help-to-buy scheme, Andy Burnham has announced.

Arriving at Labour’s annual conference, the prime minister said he was concerned by the high number of young people who have given up on home ownership because of high living costs, and wanted to change that.

The party’s first major announcement on the eve of its conference came as Mr Burnham promised a “new direction” after a decade since Brexit had resulted in “drift and division”.

He said: “Too many young people are struggling with the cost of housing, with many giving up hope of ever having a home to call their own.

“So we will step in to help more first-time buyers onto the housing ladder, especially those who can’t call on the bank of mum and dad.

“Your First Home will get them the keys to their own front door, and give builders the confidence to deliver the high-quality new homes the country needs. This Labour government is bringing back hope for people across the country.”

open image in gallery Andy Burnham speaks to the media as he and his wife Marie-France Van Heel arrive for the Labour Party Conference at the ACC Liverpool. ( PA )

Funding for the Your First Home scheme will be drawn from reprioritised existing government spending. and buyers could secure a property with a deposit of just 2.5 per cent.

A government equity loan covering 20 per cent of the property's overall value will be provided to support the purchase and will be interest-free initially to maintain affordability.

With the average UK starter home costing £230,000 according to Rightmove, buyers could provide a £5,750 deposit and access up to £46,000 in loan support.

Full details will be presented by the Chancellor John Healey at the Budget on October 28.

Housing developers will also fund running costs, which ministers hope will give the industry confidence to construct new homes.

Housing secretary Angela Rayner stated: "We’ve seen too many people priced out and giving up on the dream of ever having a home to call their own.

"This scheme will make getting on the first rung of the property ladder just that bit easier and increase access to home ownership.

open image in gallery The prime minister said he was concerned by the high number of young people who have given up on home ownership because of high living costs ( AFP via Getty Images )

She added: "For those looking for their first home, this is a Labour government that is on your side and fighting your corner.

"Your First Home will build on the lessons learned from previous schemes, while retaining the benefits, giving more families the building blocks for a better life and boosting the housing market as we turn the page on the housing crisis the Tories left behind.

"We’re delivering a new generation of equity loans in a Labour way, targeting support to those first-time buyers who need support the most and who don’t have the benefit of a large deposit from the bank of mum and dad."

In another announcement on the eve of the conference, Labour also revealed it was expanding its job guarantee scheme by giving young people on health benefits fast access to job opportunities in a bid to cut the welfare bill.

Through government funding, young people receiving health or disability support will be offered a guaranteed job three months after they start claiming benefits, down from 18 months.

Work and Pensions secretary Pat McFadden said Labour was “putting long-term sick and disabled people at the front of the queue from April next year”.

Heavy rain and powerful winds are expected to bring flash floods and extreme surf to the Hawaiian Islands over the weekend as Hurricane Nolo bears down on areas still recovering from previous storms.

Nolo was churning slowly south of Hawaii's Big Island on Saturday with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (165 kph). The storm's center was about 145 miles (235 kilometers) south of Hawaii's southernmost point and could strengthen into a potentially life-threatening and catastrophic storm through the weekend.

Forecasters warned of possible flooding and mudslides, with parts of the Big Island expected to see rainfall totals up to 20 inches (51 centimeters). Heavy rainfall also was expected on Hawaii's other islands.

“Don’t venture out if you don’t have to into the dangerous flooding environment, but also high winds. We can have trees and power lines down,” Michael Brennan, director of the National Hurricane Center, said Friday.

The humanitarian nonprofit group CORE and other partners spent the week packing and shipping supplies like camp stoves and hygiene products by air cargo from Oahu to the Big Island for a community relief hub that has been active since August's Hurricane Lala.

Residents are still recovering from Lala, which produced heavy rain and winds strong enough to sweep around 100 homes off their foundations on the Big Island.

Hawaii prepares for northern edge of Nolo

President Donald Trump on Friday approved an emergency declaration for the state of Hawaii, authorizing the Federal Emergency Management Agency to coordinate assistance from across the federal government and provide funding support for emergency measures.

Hawaii officials told residents to put together emergency kits, and the governor issued an emergency proclamation, activating hundreds of Hawaii National Guard members.

Hawaii County officials on the Big Island were urging residents in flood-prone areas to consider taking refuge at shelters being set up or other locations.

Hawaiian Electric, the state’s primary utility, said crews that had been helping restore power in Kauai after this month’s Hurricane Lowell returned to Oahu, Maui and the Big Island in preparation for the storm.

Polo is strengthening on its way to Mexico

Meanwhile, Mexico is under the threat of Hurricane Polo as it heads toward the Baja California peninsula after bringing storm conditions to the southwestern coast. Polo was producing maximum sustained winds of 155 miles per hour (249 kph) Saturday but is expected to gradually weaken before making landfall Monday.

One of the towns in Polo’s projected path is San Juanico, a small fishing community on Baja’s Pacific coast where access to basic needs is already fickle.

“Our people are concerned about this event,” said Gloriely Robles Meza, a manager at a small hotel there. “We haven’t faced such a worrying situation in many years.”

The town has only had full-time electricity for a couple of years, and it still experiences frequent outages. Without power, residents can’t refrigerate food or pump water. The closest gas station is so far away that fuel is stored and sold from tanks in the town and frequently runs out if there is high demand.

Robles Meza said the community feels left to brace itself for the storm without the help of authorities.

“We must prepare on our own — each of us protecting our homes and belongings,” she said, adding that she wished officials would preposition heavy machinery for clearing roads, along with emergency generators.

For now, she said, the only plan is to convert the local elementary school into a shelter.

“While this is important, we also have other impacts to consider,” she said, like what the town will do if it is cut off from help.

San Juanico has experienced late summer storms, but Polo feels different, said Jeffrey Westman, an American who was first drawn to the town’s world-class surf break 40 years ago and owns a property there.

“During the last couple of years, the storms have felt big and strong and scary,” said Westman, 63, who is in Europe right now but is concerned for the locals in San Juanico, particularly about their ability to receive food deliveries or reach larger grocery stores if road access is cut off.

Washed out roads could also block access to the closest medical facility, about 80 minutes away in Ciudad Constitución.

Westman said he is hopeful Polo behaves the way some past storms have, losing intensity before reaching the Baja coastline.

“A lot of times they do start petering out,” as they approach, he said. “I’m hoping that’s the case.”

___

Associated Press writers Dave Collins in Hartford, Connecticut; Gabriela Aoun Angueira in San Diego; Kathy McCormack in Concord, New Hampshire; and Hannah Schoenbaum in Salt Lake City contributed.

A respected Lib Dem MP who influenced the party strongly on equality issues has announced she will not fight the election after attempts to deselect her.

Allies of Edinburgh West MP Christine Jardine have told The Independent that she has decided to not stand at the next election as a Lib Dem because she was being forced out in favour of an ally of the party’s Scottish leader Alex Cole-Hamilton.

The 65-year-old former journalist had failed to get reselected by her constituency party’s executive committee and has decided not to push for a vote of all the members in the seat.

In a statement, Ms Jardine pointedly noted that she did not want “to expose anyone to more tension and division” by continuing to attempt to get reselected.

She said: “I have written to my local party to let them know I shall not be standing as the Scottish Liberal Democrat candidate for Edinburgh West at the next election, following the recent decision by some of the local party.

open image in gallery Christine Jardine will not fight the next election for the Lib Dems ( UK Parliament )

"I have informed them that although I am able to request a ballot of the membership, it is with a heavy heart that I have decided not to pursue this. I do not wish to expose anyone to more tension and division.

"I shall continue to represent my constituents with the care I have always sought to bring over the last nine years.

"It has been, and remains, an honour and a privilege to represent this part of the city, and to work with our fantastic communities."

A former journalist and then special adviser at the Scotland Office during the coalition government, Ms Jardine was first elected in Edinburgh West in the 2017 snap election called by Theresa May after the EU referendum.

She had previously fought the Gordon seat against former SNP leader Alex Salmond.

While she was sacked as the Lib Dem’s equalities spokesperson by party leader Sir Ed Davey for defying the party whip in a Commons vote, it is understood that he has been “very supportive” of her while she faced seselection.

A motion supporting trans rights passed at the Lib Dem conference was carried partly because of the work she had done on equalities even though she was unable to attend the conference in Brighton.

Lib Dem leader, Ed Davey, said: “Christine is a fantastic champion for Liberalism, Scotland and the people of Edinburgh.

“For me, her work on the Domestic Abuse Act stands out. She has improved things for survivors and children in ways many will never know.“I know there’s a lot more to come in this parliament too.”

The Independent has contacted Scottish Lib Dems and Mr Cole-Hamilton for comment.

ESPN analyst Kirk Herbstreit has been roasted by football fans over his “MAGA orange makeup” while covering the highly-anticipated Texas-Tennessee football matchup.

The matchup, between top-ranked Texas and No. 14-ranked Tennessee, is being played at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville with President Donald Trump in attendance.

After his College GameDay appearance on ESPN Saturday morning, Herbstreit was subsequently reporting from inside the stadium ahead of kickoff when fans noted his uneven makeup job.

“Someone tell Kirk Herbstreit make up personnel to do a better job,” one person wrote on X as another said: “Kirk HERBSTREIT looks like he has a clown face on today.”

“Kirk herbstreit needs to take his ass back to ulta and ask for a refund,” another wrote, alongside a screenshot showing the analyst’s uneven eyebrows and smattering of orange-colored makeup across his face.

open image in gallery Kirk Herbstreit’s makeup during the Texas-Tennessee game drew the attention of viewers ( Getty )

“Someone tell Kirk Herbstreit to fix his make up,” someone else chimed. Another wondered: “What’s going on with Kirk Herbstreit’s eyebrows?”

“Kirk herbstreit got his maga orange makeup on today,” another said. Trump received a mixed reaction from the crowd when he was announced at the game, with both boos and cheers being heard on the broadcast.

As the game kicked off, audio issues plagued the broadcast booth, drawing additional complaints from fans watching at home.

“It’s amazing how Kirk Herbstreit is broadcasting the game from outer space today,” one fan wrote on X while another said, “Every time Kirk Herbstreit talks, my TV sounds like a 1994 dial-up internet connection trying to load a low-res quality of a Super Nintendo game.”

open image in gallery Donald Trump's executive assistant Natalie Harp holds a laptop showing something to Trump and Senator Bill Hagerty (R-TN) during an NCAA college football game between the University of Texas and the University of Tennessee at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville ( Reuters )

Another begged Herbstreit to “just stop talking bruh your mic is cooked.”

Play-by-play announcer Chris Fowler was even heard telling Herbstreit to “be quiet for a minute” as the audio issues persisted.

The static came as Herbstreit and Fowler were discussing how Trump’s attendance could impact communications inside of the stadium.

Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian spoke earlier this week about how the president’s movements in and around the stadium impact players and coaches.

“They cut the headsets to coaches. They cut headsets for coach-to-player communication. So you have to have a plan for that, if and when it happens, and you get no warning. It just gets cut out,” Sarkisian told The Associated Press.

Ahead of Trump’s arrival at the stadium, fans were encouraged to show up early for Secret Service checks.

News.title: Red Roses triumph over New Zealand in chaotic late scenes – how it unfolded
News.content:
Just when it looked like the Red Roses’ lustre was beginning to fade, up stepped Zoe Harrison.

In one of the most dramatic finishes to an England match in recent memory, the fly-half gobbled up Amy Du Plessis’s pass to glide over the whitewash and secure a pulsating win over New Zealand.

Ever the epitome of calmness, Harrison was undeterred by the fact she had just missed what would have been a match-winning penalty from 42 metres out with the score locked at 19-19.

But after their arm-wrestle with Canada last weekend in Exeter, which finished 26-26, there was simply no way the Red Roses were going to settle for a draw for a second week running.

A year to the day since they were crowned world champions in their own back yard, England’s status as the most dominant side in the women’s game was all but confirmed by this never-say-die victory over the Black Ferns.

News.title: Russell holds his nerve to see off Verstappen and win Azerbaijan GP
News.content:
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend went the way many believed the 2026 season would play out. George Russell strolled to victory from pole, though with a little late jeopardy, whilst Kimi Antonelli’s crash in qualifying meant he had to fight his way through the field to finish fifth. That, after all, was the order of things last season.

Yet the past few days in Baku are an inversion of the season’s storyline. It is Antonelli who has been the faster driver, heading for a maiden world title at the second time of asking. Russell has been the troubled one. This was only the Briton’s third victory of the season and his first since Austria in late June. Antonelli has racked up eight wins and, before this weekend in Baku, a well-deserved 81-point lead over Russell.

Russell’s dominant and impressive run from pole to the chequered flag on Saturday is both a reminder of what he is capable of and also what might have been, had he been able to find this type of form earlier and more often. The reality, though, is that he needs to replicate this for the rest of the season to even be in with a sniff, barring a catastrophic meltdown from Antonelli. Still, Russell looked elated to have ended his barren run.

The finish was a little more tense than Russell deserved, having established a healthy lead in the first half of the race. Two late safety cars eradicated his advantage and helped put Max Verstappen’s Red Bull on his gearbox. In the end, he triumphed by just under 0.2sec and, as Antonelli finished fifth – with some help from two safety-car inducing crashes – he made up 15 points on his Mercedes team-mate. Isack Hadjar completed the podium for Red Bull after missing the past three races with a wrist injury.

News.title: Scotland’s Pocognoli era starts with encouraging signs but familiar issues in front of goal
News.content:

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

News.title: Carreras’ try-of-season contender helps Bath eclipse Harlequins
News.content:
And they kept playing, it was not until Richards scored in the 72nd minute that the game was decided. Still for Bath, a five-try victory away from home, felt like a decent return.

If they were to stand any chance of finding a way back into the game, Quins had to score first after the restart. They were rewarded for their attacking intent after running from a scrum deep in their half, with Murley cutting a brilliant line before Pedro Delgado drove over for his side’s third try.

Quins had the opportunity to further cut the deficit when first Sam Riley carried down the left wing and Cameron Anderson drove into the Bath 22. But as Quins looked to pick and go, Beno Obano and Guy Pepper combined to hold the ball up over the line.

It felt like a significant moment and when Riley was shown a yellow card for a high tackle on Obano moments later, the odds against a Quins comeback lengthened again. Yet there was something sticky about their resilience.

“I am really happy with the grit and the fight that they showed, particularly in the second half,” said Gilmore. “We had some massive defensive sets on our goal-line which we withstood. I reckon they were the moments last year that Bath would probably run in three tries really quickly and kick the score out, which is good.”

Bath emptied their bench, including the introduction of England flanker Pepper, but they could not pull away as expected in the final quarter, despite some impressive contributions by Tom de Glanville.

It was left to their line-out maul to score their first points of the second half, with Richards touching down to seal Harlequins’ fate. Still, there were enough promising glimpses to give Harlequins supporters hope that more encouraging days lie ahead.

News.title: Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges
News.content:
Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been announced.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

The charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

Of the 115 charges:

Fifty-four were for failing to provide accurate financial information from 2009-10 to 2017-18

Fourteen were for failing to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from the same period

Five were for failing to comply with Uefa’s rules from 2013-14 to 2017-18

Seven were for breaching Premier League profitability and sustainability rules from 2015-16 to 2017-18

Thirty-five were for failing to co-operate with the investigation from 2018-23.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

Case is far from being resolved

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

It would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

News.title: Britain sends team to South Sudan as country braces for Ebola
News.content:
British Ebola specialists have been deployed to South Sudan because of fears the haemorrhagic fever will spread from neighbouring Congo.

A rare form of Ebola, known as the Bundibugyo species, is spreading rapidly in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 7,800 people have caught the virus since May, 3,700 of whom have died.

To prepare for the threat of imported cases, Britain has positioned three experts in and around the South Sudanese capital, Juba. They will assist and train local authorities on infection control, set up awareness campaigns for local communities, and test people crossing the border for the virus.

The team is employed by the UK Health Security Agency’s (UKHSA) Public Health Rapid Support Team (PHRST), which is regularly sent to the epicentre of disease outbreaks overseas – for instant the cruise ship at the centre of a deadly hantavirus in the South Atlantic earlier this year.

The current Ebola outbreak is the fastest-growing ever recorded and is on course to become the largest in history, overtaking the 2014-16 West Africa Ebola outbreak, in which around 30,000 people contracted the haemorrhagic fever and roughly a third died.

Experts fear it is only a matter of time before the virus spreads to South Sudan, which shares a 500-mile border with the DRC. Thousands of people cross the frontier each day to work, attend school and trade goods, mostly fish, in lucrative markets between the two countries.

If the virus gained a foothold in South Sudan, which became the newest country on earth after severing ties with Khartoum in 2011, experts fear the consequences would be catastrophic and worsen an already dire humanitarian situation.

“It’s so variable as to where the outbreak is spreading at the moment, there are cases from some of the border towns [with South Sudan],” Ed Newman, director of the PHRST, told The Telegraph.

“There’s a feeling [Ebola could spread] any day. Maybe you could say we’ve been lucky so far,” Mr Newman said, on the sidelines of a UKHSA conference in Manchester.

News.title: Russell capitalises on Antonelli error to take Azerbaijan GP pole

Russell – who begins the weekend 81 points behind the Italian – simply has to capitalise. And he really should do. Even if Antonelli hadn’t crashed out, he has looked on a different level this weekend, dominating practice and qualifying. Russell topped Q1, Q3 and Q3, securing the 12th pole of his career with a lap which was nine tenths quicker than his best lap in Q2 and eight tenths quicker than Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, the next fastest driver. He could hardly believe it himself.

“That was a pretty decent lap,” he told his team over the radio on his cooldown lap. “How much was [the gap]?”

“Just over eight tenths to Leclerc.” came the response. “Woah!”

This has not been the easiest season for Russell, who began the year the overwhelming favourite for the title, having dominated his younger team-mate over the course of last season. So he could be forgiven for feeling proud of having done such a good job.

“It’s been a while so it definitely feels good,” he admitted. “This was probably the biggest pole margin of my whole career, including my F2 and F3 days.

“The lap felt really sweet, car’s been feeling really great this weekend. On a track like this where you can hug it, it feels amazing.”

Sports.title: Why does England badge have Three Lions on it, and has the iconic crest always been the same?
Sports.content:
LION HEARTS Why does England badge have Three Lions on it, and has the iconic crest always been the same?







Next

ENGLAND have become synonymous with the Three Lions that have been proudly displayed on their shirt for years.

The iconic Three Lions and ten red roses will once again feature as England kick off their Nations League campaign against Spain on Saturday.

An iteration of this emblem was first used in 1872, when England faced off against Scotland in the first ever football international.

It was used as the crest of the Football Association, tracing its history to King Henry I and Richard the Lionheart.

King Richard displayed banners featuring three golden lions into battle, with every English monarch following suit by incorporating this into their Royal Coat of Arms.

Interestingly, the FA had to ask for permission before England could use the Three Lions as it is officially a royal emblem.

Meanwhile, the ten red roses are thought to be a nod to the Wars of the Roses, fought between Yorkshire and Lancashire between 1455 and 1487.

This was eventually won by Henry Tudor at the Battle of Bosworth Field, taking the throne from King Richard III.

Has the badge always been the same?

There has only been one major change to the world-famous badge in the last 154 years.

A crown was originally included above the Three Lions, but this was removed in 1949 as it was difficult to differentiate between the FA and the England and Wales Cricket Board’s logo.

Another change saw a star added above the logo after England won the World Cup in 1966.

More recently, a minor cosmetic change saw the word “England” removed from above the crest in 2009.

“There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position.



“But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

“I ask you to please carefully read the statement, which we gave on Friday, and the statement we issued in February 2023. Every word matters and holds true.

Sports.content:
Man City braced for major financial blow after 115 charges verdict

Reports emerged on Friday claiming that Manchester City have been found guilty of alleged financial breaches

View Image Man City were reportedly found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges (Image: Gary Oakley/PA Wire)

Manchester City could reportedly have to deal with the loss of millions of pounds in sponsorship deals if the guilty verdict for the alleged financial breaches stands. News emerged on Friday claiming that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges that had been brought against them by the Premier League.

‌



City were first charged back in 2023, and three years later, a verdict has now emerged, but the club has always maintained their innocence and will now be expected to appeal the outcome of the case.

‌



There will be a wait to discover the full extent of any punishment that City could be forced to deal with if the guilty verdict stands, with ramifications ranging from points deductions to expulsion from the Premier League, as well as past titles being removed.

‌



A report in The Telegraph has now claimed that City face the risk of losing millions in sponsorship deals if the guilty verdict remains.

Man City chairman insists club are INNOCENT in letter after 115 charges verdict READ MORE :

Some of City's sponsors are said to be currently "examining" deals in place with the club, in the event that relegation occurs as a result of the charges.

The report claims that some of City's sponsors may hold the right to renegotiate their deal if the club are relegated from the Premier League, which would likely result in a loss in revenue.

‌



If City are relegated from the Premier League, it would also be likely that the club would not compete in the Champions League next season, which would also see the club miss out on the bonuses that come from competing in Europe’s elite cup competition.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak issued a statement on Saturday in response to the reports that the club had been found guilty of the charges, maintaining his confidence in the club's innocence.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca's agents give cryptic response to Man City 115 charges bombshell
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca's agents give cryptic response to Man City 115 charges bombshell

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was approached for a response following Manchester City being found guilty of 114 of the financial breaches they were charged with by the Premier League

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca's agents have responded (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Enzo Maresca's representatives pointed reporters in the direction of Socrates when asked for a comment on Manchester City being found guilty of 114 Premier League charges relating to financial rule breaking. The verdict of the independent commission has been long-awaited after the hearing in December 2024.

‌



City have maintained their innocence throughout the process and intend to appeal the decision. Maresca took charge of the club over the summer knowing that a decision was looming over the Etihad Stadium.

‌



Asked for a response by The Guardian, Maresca's representatives replied with a screenshot from Maresca's Instragram account. The former Chelsea and Leicester coach had posted on the social media site hours before news emerged of City's guilt.

‌



There, he had quoted the Greek Philosopher Socrates. The quote reads: “The only thing I know is that I know nothing.”

Underneath, Maresca wrote: “Time to breathe. Time to analyse. Time to learn.”

‌



City's official response suggested the process was still ongoing. In a statement, they noted that proceedings should remain strictly confidential.

“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023," they said.

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca quoted Socrates on Instagram on Friday (Image: Instagram/@maresca)

‌

“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

The statement released by City back in February 2023 noted that the club were 'surprised' by the Premier League's decision to bring charges. They also said that "The Club welcomes the review of this matter by an independent Commission, to impartially consider the comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence that exists in support of its position".

‌



While City will have the opportunity to appeal, possible sanctions could be decided on a faster timeline. Punishments could range from a fine to a points deduction or even expulsion from the Premier League.

Premier League rivals are also investigating legal action. Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham have already preserved their right to claim compensation due the loss of earnings they suffered due to City's success.

A potential £200million claim in the offing with those clubs reported to be 'planning' to launch an action.

Sports.title: Ex-Man City chairman predicts 'drastic' sanctions as Premier League rivals plan response
Sports.content:
Ex-Man City chairman predicts 'drastic' sanctions as Premier League rivals plan response

An independent commission has found Manchester City guilty of 114 of 115 charges for breaching Premier League financial rules - with an appeal set to be launched

View 2 Images Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein has had his say on the guilty verdict (Image: (Photo by Julian Finney - The FA/The FA via Getty Images))

Manchester City have been left facing a massive bill and backlash - and could be heading for an even bigger “disaster.”

‌



Rival clubs are plotting huge legal actions against the former champions after the guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules.

‌



They believe they could be due hundreds of millions in compensation if City are proven to have cost them Champions League football, commercial deals, bonuses and prize money.

‌



But City have also been warned by one of their biggest fans that dragging out a long appeal process would see the club’s already “tarnished” name damaged even further.

Former City chairman David Bernstein said: “To see all this tarnished in this way is very sad, I feel particularly bad for the wonderful supporters of the club who’ve stayed with the club through thick and thin.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“This whole process has taken too long already. So the appeal process now has to be done quickly because…you’ve got the club playing with this cloud over its head and it’s just not viable.

“The appeal process cannot go on for year after year, I think that would be a disaster. Not just for this particular case but for English football generally.”

‌



There are fears that if City launch an appeal - which was described as “inevitable’ by one executive of another club - then that could drag on because a different panel would have to be set up to hear a review of the case.

That would cast a huge shadow over the Premier League while it goes on and if it is not resolved during the course of the season then it could see City be crowned champions despite having been found guilty which would be unthinkable.

View 2 Images Man City are facing huge sanctions if their appeal is unsuccessful (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Former FA chairman Bernstein, talking to Times Radio, believes any punishment must be way beyond a fine. He added: “I can’t give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of 115 charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty.

“All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that.”

City have not confirmed anything but issued a statement insisting the process is ongoing. But this latest development has left the whole football world in meltdown.

‌



The alleged offences - they are believed to have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges - came between 2009 and 2018 during which time they became the most dominant team in English football.

Premier League rivals are certain to look at their options. Burnley made a claim against Everton in June after the Merseyside club’s PSR breach in 2021. Burnley claimed it gave them a sporting advantage and were awarded £35.1m.

‌



Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham are believed to have taken out a legal notice and reserved their Section W of the competitions rules and some estimates suggest they could be in line for £200m each.

But it is highly likely that other clubs - despite being bound by time constraints under a statute of limitations and also effectively being part of a “private members’ club” within the Premier League rules - could also attack the process and push for compensation.

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said: “I think most football fans will be feeling this is not a good moment for football as a whole and I think Manchester City fans will be feeling very anxious about what happens next.

‌



“You’ll know this is a really long standing investigation, it dates all the way back to allegations that begin in 2009. There is still a way to go with the investigation, Manchester City is contesting the charges.

“The football fans need to know the rules are applied fairly and consistently, they need to know they’re upheld and they need to know the right decision has been reached.

“We do have a way to go with this, it’s very unsettling for football fans and I hope that it can be resolved as swiftly as possible.”

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland player 'boycotts' Israel match as teammates call emergency meeting
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland player 'boycotts' Israel match as teammates call emergency meeting

Republic of Ireland are scheduled to face Israel in a Nations League match in Hungary on Sunday night, amid vocal opposition to the game taking place

View 2 Images Gavin Bazunu has informed Republic of Ireland bosses of his final decision

More Republic of Ireland players could boycott Sunday’s match with Israel after Gavin Bazunu confirmed he does not want to play in the fixture.

‌



The Bolton Wanderers goalkeeper, who is his country’s second choice, told bosses on Friday about his intention to not play, according to the Telegraph.

‌



His teammates are now considering their options and it's thought more could follow the same path throwing the UEFA Nations League match into major doubt. There have been increasingly vocal calls for Ireland to boycott the fixture, amid the backdrop of the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

‌



A UN-commissioned inquiry previously found Israel has committed genocide against Palestinians in war-torn Gaza. More than 73,000 people have been killed after Israeli military action was launched in response to the Hamas attack on the Nova Festival in southern Israel of October 7 2023, which killed approximately 1,200 people.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



An open letter from more than 160 Irish athletes urged the Irish Football Association (FAI) to withdraw from the fixture, with protests outside the team’s hotel in Dublin earlier this week.

It was expected that Ireland’s players would issue a statement at Saturday morning’s pre-match press conference. However, that was cancelled and rearranged minutes before the scheduled time, with no reason offered.

Last year, the FAI voted to submit a motion to UEFA that would have seen Israel banned from club and international competitions. The FAI cited two alleged violations of UEFA rules, including organising clubs in occupied Palestine without the permission of the Palestinian FA and the failure to enforce an effective anti-racism policy.

‌



Ireland captain Dara O’Shea made clear it was important that the opinions of all players were heard in the build-up. He said: “We’ve got to respect each other’s opinions and each other’s views and really sit down and take the time, because it deserves the time to talk about.

View 2 Images Heimir Hallgrimsson, Head Coach of Republic of Ireland (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

“It’s the main thing and it’s something that can’t be brushed over. Whatever decision that we go through as players is taken as one and everybody’s view is respected as well.”

‌



Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson elicited a response from the Israeli FA earlier this week when he said “we are not playing with genocide. We are playing against genocide. We are playing against Israel; we are not playing with Israel.”

In response the Israeli FA issued a statement which read: We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way.

“Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by the @IrelandFootball team coach. We’re not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we’re playing against the coach who embodies them.”

Article continues below

Israel are currently prohibited from playing games at home, due to security concerns, with this weekend’s match scheduled to take place in Hungary. The return fixture will also be played on neutral ground - in Serbia - amid the opposition to the game taking place.
