Sports.title: Russell soaks up pressure from Verstappen to win Azerbaijan Grand Prix | 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix report
Sports.content:
George Russell claimed his third victory of 2026 by leading every lap of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The Mercedes driver led home the Red Bull pair of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar, who rose through the field with strong pace early on.

Russell led the majority of the race until it was interrupted by a Safety Car period triggered by Alexander Albon. The Williams driver crashed out at turn five.

Almost the entire field took the opportunity to pit, after which Russell led from Piastri, Verstappen and Hadjar. Verstappen pounced on Piastri for second place at the restart, than carnage broke out behind them.

Franco Colapinto dived down the inside of turn one from a long way back and clattered into his team mate Pierre Gasly. The pair also skittled Lando Norris, who had dropped down the order earlier on by running wide at the same corner.

Remarkably, this wasn’t the only collision by a pair of team mates at the restart. Arvid Lindblad slithered wide into the sister car of Liam Lawson, tipping him into a spin, though the unimpressed Lawson was able to continue. “Man I love getting taken out by my team mate,” he remarked sarcastically. “That’s pretty sick.”

The second restart was clean and Russell led away with Verstappen close behind. Hadjar began applying pressure to Piastri and did not have to wait long for the McLaren driver to slip up. Piastri ran deep at turn one, just as Norris had earlier, and tumbled out of the points places.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Verstappen spent the final laps chasing Russell but dropped out of Overtake Mode range when the final lap began. However he closed suddenly after the pair passed the crashed Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas at turn 15. Russell reached the line less than two tenths of a second before Verstappen, while Isack Hadjar completed Red Bull’s first double podium finish for over two years.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli made slow progress initially from 16th place on the grid, losing a place on the first lap. However the Safety Car brought him within range of the front-runners, aided by the disaster for the Alpine drivers. He picked off Lewis Hamilton for fifth place on lap 43 but ran out of time to catch Charles Leclerc.

Lindblad made amends for colliding with his team mate by passing both Haas drivers in the final laps. He took Esteban Ocon as they sprinted for the line, crossing it just three hundredths of a second before his rival.

Oliver Bearman took ninth while Carlos Sainz Jnr picked up a single point in the upgraded Williams.

Sports.title: Norris says “some drivers shouldn’t be in Formula 1” after Colapinto takes him out | Formula 1
Sports.content:
A dejected Lando Norris said some drivers on the grid should not be in Formula 1 after he was taken out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The reigning world champion was involved in a three-car collision at the restart of the race. The crash began when Franco Colapinto arrived too quickly on the inside of turn one, hit his team mate Pierre Gasly, who in turn hit Norris’s car.

“In end of the day I just got taken out,” said Norris, “so just some drivers that shouldn’t be in Formula 1 to be honest.”

Colapinto received a 10-second time penalty for the collision. Alpine recently renewed Colapinto’s contract to drive for the team again next year.

Norris endured a frustrating race as he said he lacked straight-line speed. He also went off at turn one earlier in the race.

“I just was slow, struggling a lot in the straights,” he said. “You saw how quickly everyone came past me, so it’s just an impossible race out there for me from that side in straight line speed today, so hopefully we get that fixed for next time.”

Norris was also quoted calling for race bans to be imposed on drivers who cause similar crashes. However others did not agree with his point of view.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“I think that’s too harsh, personally,” said George Russell. “I think Safety Car restarts, cold tyres, a very small mistake can have big consequences. From what I saw today, that’s what it looked like.

“It was a small error that had a big consequence. I think, personally, race bans should come from drivers intentionally doing something very dangerous and very reckless. So I think it was unfortunate.”

Max Verstappen agreed “a race ban probably is a bit much” for this kind of incident.

“That happens. A small mistake or misjudgement, you lock up, it’s on the inside, low grip, and, of course, then I guess it’s a bit unfortunate that it involves so many cars.”

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Calls Russell, But Who Buys It?
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson wants to unify with Gary Antuanne Russell at 140 pounds. Russell has talked about letting the fight grow. The trouble is that Russell has done little to make it bigger, and a second belt may not be enough to sell Shakur’s next event.

“Gary Antuanne Russell let’s unify,” Shakur posted on X.

It is an easy callout to make. Russell holds the WBA title, so a win would add another belt to Shakur’s collection. But Shakur’s WBO mandatory is due in November. If he wants Russell first, his team needs to pursue the fight and get the WBO’s approval. Five words online do not settle either piece of business.

Russell’s talk of letting the fight marinate is harder to understand. He did not look impressive against Alberto Puello or Andy Hiraoka, and he has little presence between fights. He is not drawing casual fans in through interviews, personality, or frequent social media posts. What would another year of waiting do for him?

That matters if Turki Alalshikh is asked to pay for the fight. Russell brings a title and a dangerous inside game, but he is not a name that draws fans by himself. At 140, there are few popular fighters to help sell a major event. A unification sounds good; it still needs an audience. Turki may prefer to put Shakur in with someone fans are eager to see test him.

Russell would have to provide that test in the ring. He has the hands to hurt Shakur up close, but reaching him is the problem. Shakur will use his jab and the full canvas rather than trade in the pocket. If Russell follows instead of cutting off the ring, this could become twelve frustrating rounds for him and for the crowd.

Shakur has named an opponent with a belt. Russell says the fight needs more time. Neither has explained how waiting turns it into a bigger attraction. If they want it, make an offer and see whether anyone is willing to pay for it.

Sports.title: Turki Should Walk If Hearn Prices Out Fury–Joshua
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn has a reason to fight Dana White’s involvement in Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua that goes beyond AJ’s contract. If White helps stage the biggest British fight in years at a Cardiff stadium, what does that leave Matchroom doing?

Hearn says White cannot have a promotional role under Joshua’s agreement. Yet White’s name appeared in the fight announcement, and he says he is working on Turki Alalshikh’s side.

“I am not involved in either side of this thing. I’m involved on the Turki side,” White told Sky Sports. “The fighters are getting paid. Everybody’s got to make some money.”

That distinction may be crucial to a lawyer. To fans watching White promote a December 11 event in Cardiff, it will look like he got onto Hearn’s biggest home turf. Hearn has spent years building Matchroom around fights like this. He is hardly going to smile while a rival takes a prominent role and Matchroom looks like AJ’s management team.

Turki has a problem of his own. If settling the dispute requires a large additional payment to Joshua and Matchroom, he has to ask what he is buying. The fight was already agreed. Paying substantially more because the promotional credits are contested would tell other promoters that a signed deal can become the opening round of another negotiation.

We do not know what Hearn has requested, or even if he has put a number on accepting White’s role. It would be unfair to call his price excessive without seeing it. But Turki does not have to pay any price simply to spare everyone the embarrassment of a canceled fight.

AJ has leverage because Fury–Joshua remains a massive attraction. His recent work in the ring gives him considerably less. The audience is paying to see these two names finally meet, not to watch Joshua prove he is still the best heavyweight. Walking away would also cost AJ a payday that another opponent is unlikely to match.

Fury has already shown how he would sell a collapse. During the earlier dispute over the venue, he blamed Joshua and Hearn for holding up the fight and talked about moving on. If this argument kills it, Hearn can point to the contract, while Fury can tell fans AJ’s side stopped them from fighting. Neither account would settle what actually happened.

Turki should try to make Fury–Joshua happen. It is bigger than the available alternatives, and replacing it this close to December would be difficult. But if the cost of resolving White’s role becomes unreasonable, he can spend his money on another major fight. Hearn has every right to defend Matchroom’s deal. Turki has every right to decide when defending it has become too expensive.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn’s Coffee Mug Cannot Close Fury Joshua Deal
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn picked an interesting morning to show off his coffee mug. With Tyson Fury claiming his fight with Anthony Joshua could be called off, Hearn posted a sunny view of the water and a cup declaring, “I got 99 problems but closing deals ain’t one.”

It is a good line for a promoter. It is a harder sell when the company broadcasting the fight says Dana White will help promote it, while Hearn insists White cannot be involved. Netflix lists the December 11 Cardiff fight and names White alongside The Ring in its promotion.

Hearn says that arrangement conflicts with the agreement he has for Joshua. Netflix Tudum

That is the problem the mug cannot cover up. Hearn represents one of the two fighters, but the money and the broadcast come from outside Matchroom. He can object to White’s role, and his contractual objection may be valid. He cannot settle the argument by sounding certain in an interview or posting a clever picture.

White knows it, too. He has made a public contest out of his involvement, daring Hearn to stop him. Hearn’s “Netflix didn’t get the memo” response may please people who already dislike White. To everyone waiting for the fight, it sounds like the parties who announced it still disagree about who is running it.

Fury has gone further, accusing Hearn and Joshua of trying to pull out. That is Fury’s claim, not proof that Joshua intends to walk away. Joshua has not publicly taken up Hearn’s fight with White in the same fashion. His silence gives us no way to know what he thinks privately, but it does make Hearn look isolated in a dispute being fought largely through microphones and social media.

Frank Warren has avoided making himself the center of this particular argument. That does not mean he has no interests of his own. It means the public sees one side working with White while Hearn is explaining why White should not be there. The contrast does Hearn no favors.

If Fury–Joshua falls apart, Hearn will still have a business, and Joshua will still have money. Joshua would also lose a huge payday. British fans would lose the fight they have spent more than a decade waiting to watch. They have heard enough from promoters about what is agreed, who holds the contract, and whose name belongs on the poster.

Hearn’s mug says closing deals is easy. Fans would probably settle for seeing this one survive until December 11.

Sports.title: Christian Mbilli Sees Canelo Alvarez’s Power Slipping
Sports.content:
Christian Mbilli thinks Canelo Alvarez has lost some power, and the results give him a case. Canelo has not stopped an opponent since Caleb Plant in 2021. His next eight fights all went the distance, including losses to Dmitry Bivol and Terence Crawford. Mbilli believes October 31 is the right time to face him.

“He’s old now, but still very dangerous, and he has very good power. Very, very good counterpunch. And I think it’s the best time for me to have this fight,” Mbilli told DAZN interviewer Todd Grisham. Asked what weakness he could exploit, Mbilli added: “I think now his power is going down a little bit, but he’s still dangerous. He’s still competitive, but I think five years ago, he was at a different level. But now, he’s a little bit down, I think.”

Canelo’s stoppage drought does not prove his punches no longer hurt. It may say as much about how often he throws them. Against Crawford, he had to chase a target who kept changing position. He spent energy resetting his feet and reacting to feints, often without getting close enough to land.

Mbilli would make Canelo work in a different way. He comes forward throwing combinations and attacks the body. If he can keep Canelo defending for long stretches, Canelo may have less energy to put behind his counters. A hard punch here and there will buy him little rest if Mbilli takes it and goes straight back to work.

There’s a catch for Mbilli: getting close enough to work Canelo’s body means walking into his counters. Derevyanchenko caught Mbilli with right hands even after tearing his left biceps. Canelo will spot those same openings if Mbilli keeps coming in with his head on the center line.

Mbilli has to make Canelo defend without giving him easy shots in return. Dig to the body, stay close, and keep punching when Canelo wants a breather. If Mbilli takes too many clean counters on the way in, though, that nonstop pace won’t last.

Sports.title: Jermall Charlo Calls October Fight His Last Run
Sports.content:
Jermall Charlo is talking about a third world title while leaving the door open to retirement. The 36-year-old former champion at 154 and 160 pounds called his October 17 fight with Koen Mazoudier part of “the last run” during a media scrum for the Las Vegas card.

“This the last run. I’m putting all my effort into it,” Jermall said. “If God wants me to keep going, I’ll keep going. But at this point, I don’t have nothing to prove. I’ve completed every task, and I’m just ready to, you know, go on the other side of boxing.”

Charlo wants another fight before the end of 2026 and mentioned the vacant WBO super middleweight title. That sounds ambitious from a fighter who has competed only three times from 2021 onward. His last bout was against Thomas LaManna in May 2025.

He said he has spent roughly 26 weeks in camp, partly because his July fight with Mazoudier fell through. That does not mean his body is breaking down. It does make the proposed quick return a question worth asking: after years of long breaks, can Charlo fight in October and get back into the ring before January?

The vacant belt is another tempting shortcut. Charlo did not say he would avoid a champion or a leading contender, and there is no evidence he has been promised a title shot. But beating Mazoudier would hardly settle his standing among Christian Mbilli, Osleys Iglesias and the other serious fighters at 168. A vacant title opportunity based chiefly on his former status would leave that question unanswered.

Charlo is also fighting beneath Sebastian Fundora’s title defense at The Cosmopolitan, a smaller stage than the one he once occupied. His long absences help explain the change without proving what networks or promoters think of his drawing power.

Jermall hasn’t said when he’ll retire. But if this is his last run, he needs to face a serious contender soon. Beating Mazoudier would get him fighting again; his next opponent would show how serious he is about winning a title at 168.

One loss might be enough for Charlo to walk away. He is already saying he has nothing left to prove and has completed everything he set out to do. If a hard fight goes against him, will he want to take the punishment and spend another year working his way back to a title shot?

Sports.title: Abel Sanchez Questions David Benavidez’s Cieslak Fight
Sports.content:
David Benavidez spent years waiting for Canelo Alvarez while he had the size to compete at light heavyweight. Now trainer Abel Sanchez is questioning why, after finally moving up, Benavidez is headed toward Michal Cieslak instead of making a stronger push for the fights he says he wants.

“He’s got to start to eliminate these guys,” Sanchez said in the interview. “He can’t keep going calling guys out.”

Sanchez wants Benavidez to beat opponents who would strengthen his claim to Dmitry Bivol or Artur Beterbiev, and he thinks Benavidez’s team should spend money to make a major fight possible.

The lost years at 168 pounds make that criticism sting. Benavidez stayed there chasing Canelo and left without the fight. He had the size to move up earlier and build his position at 175, where wins over leading contenders would have given him a stronger claim on Bivol or Beterbiev. Instead, he waited for a fight Canelo never gave him.

Cruiserweight is now producing a familiar argument. Benavidez wants Jai Opetaia, but Cieslak comes first as a WBC title opponent. “He’s fighting somebody that nobody knows,” Sanchez said.

That is harsh on Cieslak, who has earned his belt, but it gets to the career question: how much does that win add to Benavidez’s standing beside a victory over one of the division’s leading fighters?

The Opetaia fight has also acquired a longer explanation than fans expected. Opetaia signed with Zuffa, and his IBF title became the subject of a sanctioning dispute after its officials withdrew approval for his Brandon Glanton bout; that is separate from Benavidez’s decision to fight Cieslak. Benavidez and Opetaia have expressed interest in fighting, but interest alone does not put them in the ring.

Sanchez’s argument has a weak spot: money cannot always free Bivol or Beterbiev from their own commitments. Benavidez also took a serious risk against David Morrell, so it would be unfair to treat every opponent on his record as an easy choice.

Abel is still asking the right question about timing. Benavidez already spent years waiting for Canelo. If Cieslak leads directly to Opetaia, the cruiserweight move will have produced a major fight. If that fight drifts away too, another belt will be a thin return for more years spent chasing names.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Let Robeisy Ramírez Take Control
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson had Robeisy Ramírez figured out for one round. In the second round of their Olympic final on August 20, 2016, Shakur made him miss, caught him with cleaner shots and won every judge’s card. Then, with the gold medal one round away, he stopped doing enough of what had worked.

Robeisy took the split decision in Rio. It was his second Olympic gold, after winning at flyweight in London four years earlier. Shakur, just 19, went home with silver. It remains the last official loss of his boxing career. Ramírez had taken the first round on all three cards by getting close and punching in bursts.

Shakur changed the fight in the second. He gave himself more room to see Ramírez coming and picked his shots as the Cuban stepped in. He was boxing defensively, but he was making Ramírez pay for trying to close the distance.

In the third, Shakur tried to keep things quiet. He later said he was exhausted and had lost a lot of weight to make the 56 kilogram limit. He thought he could get through the round and win the decision. Ramírez fought as if he knew he had to take it. Shakur still made him miss, but the counters came less often.

Ramírez kept coming forward, forcing exchanges while Shakur backed away or tried to hold. Shakur recalled trying to grab him during the final 15 or 20 seconds as Ramírez threw punches. Two judges gave the round to Ramírez.

That’s a hard way to lose because Shakur had already shown he had an answer. He did not need to stand still and trade with Ramírez. He needed to keep landing the shots that had interrupted those attacks in the second. Instead, he tried to protect a lead the judges had not given him. Shakur did not blame the scoring afterward. He knew Ramírez had finished well.

The criticism is simpler than any argument about the judges: when the fight needed one more good round from him, Robeisy was the one doing more to win it.

Stevenson went on to win world titles across multiple divisions, and he has said losing in Rio helped make him a better fighter. That final is still difficult to forget. For one round, he showed he could beat Ramírez to the punch. In the last, he gave Robeisy too much time to punch first.

Sports.title: Mannix Sees Shakur Stevenson Stopping Manny Pacquiao
Sports.content:
Chris Mannix thinks Shakur Stevenson would stop Manny Pacquiao if they fight. Sergio Mora agrees and hates the matchup. That is a startling amount of confidence in a stoppage from two men discussing a fighter who usually wins by making opponents miss.

“I hate that fight,” Mora said on Boxing with Mannix and Mora. He called Stevenson a “pound-for-pound cheetah with boxing gloves” and questioned why Pacquiao would take this fight at nearly 50. Mannix pictured Shakur catching Pacquiao repeatedly as he attacks. Mora went further, comparing the potential punishment to Larry Holmes beating an aging Muhammad Ali.

The age concern is fair, but the stoppage talk is harder to buy. Shakur’s lack of power is only half the problem with the prediction. His first priority is avoiding punches. He lands, moves, and makes opponents start over rather than staying in range to build an attack. That approach can win rounds convincingly, but it gives a hurt fighter time to recover.

To stop Pacquiao, Shakur would likely have to hold his position after landing and throw again while Pacquiao is close enough to answer. That is a real gamble against a southpaw who can still fire fast combinations from unusual angles. Shakur may be skilled enough to outbox him, but Mannix and Mora are asking him to take chances he has spent his career avoiding.

Mora’s Holmes comparison takes the prediction into melodrama. Holmes was a heavyweight who hurt Ali with sustained offense. Shakur generally chooses the safer shot and steps away. He might outbox Pacquiao, but predicting that he pins him to the ropes for a prolonged beating asks Shakur to fight differently from the man we have watched.

A move toward 147 pounds adds another question. Shakur has not shown much stopping power against lightweights. Carrying more weight against Pacquiao would hardly make him a heavier puncher overnight. Pacquiao’s age may slow his attacks, but Shakur still has to give him openings if he intends to stand close enough to force a stoppage.

Mannix cautioned that the fight may never happen. He noted that Pacquiao has been linked to plenty of matchups that went nowhere. Shakur would gain attention and a famous name from it, but a win over a nearly 50-year-old Pacquiao would tell us less about his standing than a fight with a leading opponent of his own generation.

The idea that Shakur Stevenson suddenly morphs into an offensive power puncher capable of stopping anyone, let alone Manny Pacquiao, is unrealistic given what he’s shown during his professional and amateur career.

To score a stoppage when you lack one-punch power, you have to sit down on your punches, hold your ground in the pocket, and commit to sustained combinations. Shakur’s entire nervous system is wired to do the exact opposite. The second real heat comes his way, his instinct is to reset, step back, and look for an exit route. That survival reflex makes him difficult to look good against, but it completely removes any possibility of him breaking down a durable opponent.

Cuba’s Robeisy Ramirez exposed the foundational flaw in Shakur’s game in the Olympic finals in Rio de Janeiro. When Ramirez stepped to him, closed the distance, and made him uncomfortable with genuine spite and power, Shakur retreated into his shell. He did not bite down on his mouthpiece and trade. He looked for survival space, let the rounds slip away, and cried in the back after the decision went against him.

The exact same allergic reaction to contact surfaced in the pros against Edwin De Los Santos. The moment Shakur felt De Los Santos had legitimate dynamite in his hands, he shut down the offense entirely, threw single-digit punches a round, and spent thirty-six minutes in full retreat. If a limited puncher like De Los Santos can turn Shakur into a track star, imagine what happens when he feels the straight left hand of a seasoned welterweight legend who comes forward throwing in flurries.

If Shakur tries to stand in the pocket to prove Mannix right, he walks into potential problems. Pacquiao, even past his absolute prime, thrives against opponents who give him stationary targets in mid-range. To stop Pacquiao, Shakur would have to absorb sharp, explosive counters from strange angles. Nothing in Shakur’s professional career suggests his chin or his mindset can tolerate that kind of trade-off.

He would take two clean punches to land three keep-away shots, realize the return fire is too dangerous, and immediately climb right back on his bicycle. Mannix is dreaming if he thinks Shakur has the firepower or the stomach to force a referee to step in. There’s nothing wrong with that style, but it’s not going to be enough to knock out Pacquiao.

Ghana News.title: Guinness Ghana DJ Awards 2026 Pub Fest celebrates Ghana’s DJ culture as Accra turns up the energy
Ghana News.content:
The road to the 2026 Guinness Ghana DJ Awards, powered by Smirnoff, is gathering pace, with the Pub Fest tour bringing Ghana’s DJ culture to audiences across the country ahead of the grand finale on December 4.

The latest stop was Accra, where DJs, entertainers and music lovers gathered at Purple Pub on Friday for a night of music, performances and entertainment.

The Accra edition follows Pub Fest stops in Winneba, Takoradi and Berekum, each adding to the growing excitement around this year’s awards and taking the celebration beyond the capital.

At Purple Pub, DJ Wallpaper, DJ Juicy, DJ Coleda and DJ Raya were among the DJs who took turns behind the decks, while DJ Mark, DJ Kiss and DJ Dhon K also delivered incredible performances.

There was a particular spotlight on the women behind the decks. DJ Coleda, the Ghana DJ Awards Scratch DJ of the Year, brought her technical skills and stage presence to the event, while DJ Raya added her own energy to a line-up reflecting the growing presence of female DJs in Ghana’s music and nightlife scene.

One of the night’s highlights came when Ghana’s finest hypeman, Merqury Quaye, joined DJ Juicy on stage for a lively set that had the crowd responding as the evening gathered momentum.

The event also attracted notable figures from Ghana’s entertainment industry, including DJ Lord OTB, the reigning Hypeman of the Year, and Kojo Manuel. Actress Nana Adjoa Lovia hosted the evening.

A separate highlight was the Fiesta Condoms GH₵1,000 cash-prize activation, which gave patrons an opportunity to win cash while enjoying the music and entertainment. The activation formed part of Fiesta’s engagement with audiences during the Pub Fest.

The Pub Fest is a key part of the build-up to the 2026 Guinness Ghana DJ Awards, organised by Merqury Republic under the theme “All Out”.

The tour is taking the awards experience into different cities, giving audiences the opportunity to connect with DJs and the culture that will ultimately converge at the main ceremony.

The awards are powered by Smirnoff, with Fiesta Condoms and BrainWise Omega 3 as sponsors. Joy Prime TV is the lead media partner, with support from WatsUp TV, MX24, PLUZZ FM, Hitz FM and Revolve Media.

As the Pub Fest moves from city to city, each stop adds another chapter to the countdown. DJs are connecting with audiences in their communities, nightlife venues are becoming part of the awards-season experience, and anticipation is building towards the night when Ghana’s DJ industry comes together.

Next stop is Hohoe in the Volta Region, where the Pub Fest will continue its journey.

From Winneba to Takoradi, Berekum and Accra, the tour has already created a growing trail of excitement. Hohoe now gets its turn before the journey heads towards its ultimate destination.

On Friday, December 4, 2026, the roadshow gives way to the main Guinness Ghana DJ Awards, bringing DJs, artistes, industry professionals and fans together for the culmination of the 2026 awards season.

Every city is a stop. Every beat is part of the build-up. And it all leads to December 4.

Ghana News.title: 10th woman found dead in South Africa’s string of killings
Ghana News.content:
Screenshot

South African police on Saturday found another body in Ekurhuleni, east of Johannesburg, bringing to 10 the number of women found dead in the municipality over the past two months.

The discovery adds to growing concern over violence against women in a country long plagued by violent crime, while police work to establish whether the killings are connected.

The semi-naked body was found near a cemetery in the Tembisa township, police said.

"At this stage, we can only confirm the discovery of the body. Crime scene management and all the necessary role players are currently on the scene," police spokeswoman Brigadier Brenda Muridili said.

Provincial police chief Tommy Mthombeni said the victim appeared to have been stoned to death, and a post-mortem examination would be conducted to determine the cause of death.

"We have put highly capable investigators on this case," he told reporters at the scene, vowing to find those responsible for the killings.

The nine other victims were mostly in their 20s and 30s, with some found stripped of their clothes and showing signs of sexual assault.

The first victim, a 37-year-old woman, was found naked and bound with cable ties on July 15. A suspect was arrested two days later.

Two other suspects, women aged 31 and 38, were arrested in connection with the ninth victim and charged on Monday.

Police have said that killing may have stemmed from a relationship-related matter.

Police have offered a 400,000 rand ($25,000) reward for information leading to the arrest of the killer or killers, while the Democratic Alliance, South Africa's second-largest political party, has put up a further $31,000.

Gender-based violence is endemic in South Africa, despite years of government pledges to tackle the problem and the declaration of gender-based violence as a national disaster.

Last week, the South African government said the national Gender-Based Violence (GBV) Command Centre received 6,782 distress calls between September 1 and 16, an average of 424 a day.

That was a 21 percent increase from the same period in August, when the centre averaged 350 calls a day.

South Africa, a nation of 62 million people, has one of the world's highest murder rates, with more than 60 killings a day on average.

Ghana News.title: French Embassy trains Ghana Police CTU in counter-terrorism operations
Ghana News.content:
The French Embassy in Ghana has trained personnel of the Counter Terrorism Unit (CTU) of the Ghana Police Service in a two-week intensive workshop aimed at strengthening Ghana’s counter-terrorism response.

The workshop formed part of ongoing security cooperation between France and Ghana and focused on building the capacity of CTU personnel, equipping officers with modern counter-terrorism operational skills and improving preparedness against evolving threats in the West African sub-region.

Over the two weeks, participants underwent intensive tactical and operational training designed to strengthen their effectiveness in counter-terrorism operations.

‘A certificate is not a capability’

Addressing the graduands at the closing ceremony, Director-General of Special Duties, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCOP) Raymond Ali Adofiem, cautioned the officers against complacency, stressing that true competence goes beyond certification.

“To our participants, congratulations! But remember, a certificate is not a capability. Continue to train, practise, rehearse, share what you have learned, maintain your fitness, equipment and discipline. Do not wait for an emergency to discover whether you are prepared,” he said.

“Take the knowledge, take the discipline, take the responsibility, return to your teams and make them better,” he added.

DCOP Adofiem also expressed gratitude to the French government for its sustained support to Ghana’s security sector.

“The Government of France, the Embassy, and the team, we say merci beaucoup for sustaining this important partnership to counter terrorism departments and their instructors.”

Trainees express appreciation

In appreciation of the support, the trainees presented the French officials who facilitated the training with traditional smocks, known as fugu, and caps.

The gesture, rooted in Ghanaian culture, symbolised gratitude and friendship between the two countries.

Officials at the ceremony described the training as successful, citing the discipline and commitment demonstrated by the officers throughout the programme.

Ghana News.title: UPSA uncovers mass results manipulation involving 178 students, over 500 results compromised
Ghana News.content:
Screenshot

The University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA) has uncovered a major results manipulation scheme involving 178 students, with more than 500 academic results altered in the university’s system.

The Vice Chancellor, Prof Kwaku Mensah Mawutor, disclosed this during the university’s 18th Congregation, describing it as a serious and unfortunate incident.

According to him, some students and other individuals breached the university’s system and manipulated students’ academic results.

“Some unscrupulous students and some unscrupulous individuals breached our system by hijacking our system and changing results in our system,” Prof Mawutor said.

He said investigations had identified the culprits and established that “over 500 results were changed by 178 students.”

Prof Mawutor said some of the students subsequently admitted to paying individuals to alter their results, while others confessed to collecting money from colleagues to facilitate the manipulation.

“After the investigations, a number of them came to confess that indeed, they paid money to some unscrupulous people to change their results. Others also denied, while others confessed that they collected monies from their colleagues,” he said.

He described the development as unacceptable, particularly for an institution such as UPSA.

“This is highly unacceptable, especially at UPSA,” Prof Mawutor stressed.

The Vice Chancellor further disclosed that some of the students implicated in the results manipulation were scheduled to graduate at the university’s 18th Congregation.

However, their graduation has been withheld indefinitely to allow investigations and disciplinary processes to continue.

“Some of these culprits were supposed to graduate, but due to the hard work of our ISTD team and the investigative committee, we have withheld their graduation until further notice,” he said.

Prof Mawutor said the incident was not entirely new to the university but noted that the scale of the latest case was significant.

“This is a very, very unfortunate incident, which to me is not the first time, but this time, the magnitude is very, very significant,” he said.

He commended the university’s Information Systems and Technology Directorate (ISTD) team and the investigative committee for uncovering the manipulation and helping identify those involved.

Ghana News.title: Sylvester Mensah urges Latenu FM to promote trade, export opportunities in Ga
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of Ghana EXIM Bank, Sylvester Adinam Mensah, has proposed working with a community radio station in La to provide information on business growth, trade and export opportunities in the Ga language.

Speaking as the Special Guest of Honour at Latenu FM’s 10th anniversary celebration on Saturday, Mr Mensah urged the station to use its platform to highlight local entrepreneurs and help listeners understand the business and financing opportunities available to them.

“Use your platform to celebrate local entrepreneurs, to explain opportunities of financing and trade, and to inspire young people to create, not only to seek jobs,” he said.

Mr Mensah, a former MP for La Dadekotopon, said he was willing to explore how the station and institutions such as Ghana EXIM Bank could work together to make business information more accessible to local communities.

“I extend an open hand. Let us find ways for [the station] and institutions like EXIM to bring information about business growth and export opportunities to our people in our own language,” he said.

He praised the station for using Ga in its programmes over the past decade, saying community radio also provided local businesses with an avenue to reach customers in a language they understood.

Mr Mensah said the initiative should not be limited to the Ga language, but could also be extended to other Ghanaian languages to help disseminate important national information to a wider audience.

The station marked its anniversary with a ceremony at which it presented awards to individuals recognised for their contributions to communities in La and the wider Ga traditional area.

Ghana News.title: Ga language under threat of decline as children shy away from speaking it – Sylvester Mensah
Ghana News.content:
Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Export-Import Bank (GEXIM), Sylvester Adinam Mensah

The Chief Executive Officer of Ghana EXIM Bank, Sylvester Adinam Mensah, has warned that the Ga language is coming under growing pressure, with some children hesitant to speak it and others unable to speak it at all.

Speaking as the Special Guest of Honour at the 10th anniversary celebration of Latenu Radio in La on Saturday, Mr Mensah said the increasingly cosmopolitan nature of Accra made it even more important for families and community institutions to pass the language on to younger generations.

“Many of our children understood it, but hesitated to speak it. Some cannot speak it at all,” he said.

The former La Dadekotopon MP said language was central to a people’s knowledge, identity and sense of belonging.

“Language is not just a way of speaking. It is a way of seeing,” he told the gathering.

“A people who lose their language slowly lose their memory. And a people without memory can easily lose their way,” he added.

Mr Mensah praised the station for using Ga in its news, music and discussions over the past decade.

He urged the station to sustain that effort and develop programmes that could help people who had lost the ability to speak Ga to learn or reconnect with the language.

The station marked its anniversary with a ceremony at which it presented awards to individuals recognised for their contributions to communities in La and the wider Ga traditional area.

Ghana News.title: ‘Let every Ga child you raise know the Ga language and story’ – Sylvester Mensah
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of Ghana EXIM Bank, Sylvester Adinam Mensah, has called on Ga traditional authorities and parents to make greater efforts to teach children the Ga language and the history of their communities.

Speaking at the 10th anniversary celebration of community radio station Latenu FM in La on Saturday, September 25, the former La Dadekotopon MP expressed concern that some children understood Ga but hesitated to speak it, while others could not speak the language at all.

“Language is not just a way of speaking. It is a way of seeing,” he said.

Recalling the stories, songs and proverbs passed down by earlier generations, Mr Mensah added: “They were passing on wisdom. They were passing on identity. They were passing on pride.”

He urged Latenu FM to consider programmes that would help young people learn Ga and discover the history of their towns, institutions and local figures.

“Let no child grow up … without knowing the story of the land beneath their feet,” he said.

Mr Mensah praised the station for keeping the Ga language on the airwaves over the past decade and encouraged it to expand its programmes to podcasts, streaming platforms and social media to reach younger listeners, including those living abroad.

“You have reminded our young that our language is not old-fashioned. It is beautiful, it is modern, and it belongs to them,” he said.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
